# Broader ML — hands-on ladder

Classical ML through generative and geometric deep learning, built from scratch
before reaching for libraries. Each part carries a practical-lab reference; the
last part bridges into ignite-catalog.

Run a rung with `ladder run <id>` (for example `ladder run A1 --help`), and see
progress with `ladder status`.

## 0. Setup

*one shared repo, mirrors the RL ladder scaffolding*

**Lab:** [lightning-hydra-template — structural reference](https://github.com/ashleve/lightning-hydra-template)

- **01.** Repo scaffolding — uv-managed Python env, folder structure mirroring this ladder 1:1
- **02.** Shared eval/plotting harness package used across all parts
- **03.** W&B (or equivalent) run tracking wired in from part A onward
- **04.** Cargo workspace stub reserved for later Rust/Candle ports, tied to [[ignite-catalog]]

## A. Classical ML from scratch

*numpy only — no sklearn*

**Lab:** [Stanford CS229 problem sets](https://cs229.stanford.edu/)

Folder: `parts/a_classical/`

- **A1.** Linear & logistic regression via batch/mini-batch gradient descent — `parts/a_classical/a1_linear_logistic_regression.py`
- **A2.** Decision tree + random forest from scratch (Gini/entropy splits, bagging) — `parts/a_classical/a2_trees_and_forests.py`
- **A3.** k-means and PCA from scratch, compared against each other on the same toy dataset — `parts/a_classical/a3_kmeans_and_pca.py`
- **A4.** Minimal gradient-boosting implementation, benchmarked against XGBoost — `parts/a_classical/a4_gradient_boosting.py`

## B. Deep learning foundations

**Lab:** [karpathy/micrograd — autodiff reference implementation](https://github.com/karpathy/micrograd)

Folder: `parts/b_deep_learning/`

- **B1.** Scalar autodiff engine (micrograd-style) plus a tiny MLP trained on it — `parts/b_deep_learning/b1_autodiff_engine.py`
- **B2.** MLP on MNIST — manual backprop, then repeat with PyTorch autograd and diff the gradients — `parts/b_deep_learning/b2_mlp_mnist.py`
- **B3.** CNN on CIFAR-10 with a batchnorm/dropout ablation — `parts/b_deep_learning/b3_cnn_cifar10.py`
- **B4.** ResNet block implementation, trained on CIFAR-10/100 — `parts/b_deep_learning/b4_resnet_blocks.py`
- **B5.** Optimizer bake-off — SGD vs Adam vs AdamW, with LR-schedule comparison — `parts/b_deep_learning/b5_optimizer_bakeoff.py`

## C. Sequence models & attention

**Lab:** [Annotated Transformer / nanoGPT](https://nlp.seas.harvard.edu/annotated-transformer/)

Folder: `parts/c_sequence_attention/`

- **C1.** Char-level RNN/LSTM language model — `parts/c_sequence_attention/c1_char_rnn.py`
- **C2.** Seq2seq with attention on a toy translation task — `parts/c_sequence_attention/c2_seq2seq_attention.py`
- **C3.** Transformer from scratch (attention, positional encoding, causal masking) — `parts/c_sequence_attention/c3_transformer_from_scratch.py`
- **C4.** Fine-tune a small ViT on a custom image-classification task — `parts/c_sequence_attention/c4_vit_finetune.py`

## D. Self-supervised & representation learning

**Lab:** [lightly-ai — contrastive-learning reference implementations](https://github.com/lightly-ai/lightly)

Folder: `parts/d_self_supervised/`

- **D1.** SimCLR-style contrastive pretraining on CIFAR-10 — `parts/d_self_supervised/d1_simclr_pretraining.py`
- **D2.** Masked autoencoder (MAE) on a small image dataset — `parts/d_self_supervised/d2_masked_autoencoder.py`
- **D3.** Linear probing of the learned representations against a supervised baseline — `parts/d_self_supervised/d3_linear_probing.py`

## E. Generative models

**Lab:** [lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch — diffusion reference](https://github.com/lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch)

Folder: `parts/e_generative/`

- **E1.** VAE on MNIST/FashionMNIST — `parts/e_generative/e1_vae.py`
- **E2.** DCGAN on a small image dataset — `parts/e_generative/e2_dcgan.py`
- **E3.** DDPM diffusion model from scratch — `parts/e_generative/e3_ddpm.py`
- **E4.** Compare sample quality and training stability across VAE, GAN, and diffusion — `parts/e_generative/e4_generative_comparison.py`

## F. Geometric & equivariant nets

*ties directly to your algebraic topology / equivariant cohomology background*

**Lab:** [escnn — equivariant CNN library, and PyTorch Geometric tutorials](https://github.com/QUVA-Lab/escnn)

Folder: `parts/f_geometric/`

- **F1.** Rotation-equivariant CNN on a rotated-MNIST task, compared against a standard CNN — `parts/f_geometric/f1_equivariant_cnn.py`
- **F2.** GCN and GraphSAGE on a node-classification benchmark (Cora/PubMed) — `parts/f_geometric/f2_gcn_graphsage.py`

## G. Scaling & systems

*bridges into ignite-catalog*

**Lab:** [PyTorch mixed-precision & profiler docs](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/amp_examples.html)

Folder: `parts/g_scaling_systems/`

- **G1.** Fit your own scaling-law curve (loss vs. params/data/compute) on a small model family — `parts/g_scaling_systems/g1_scaling_law_fit.py`
- **G2.** Mixed-precision + gradient-accumulation training, profiled for throughput and memory — `parts/g_scaling_systems/g2_mixed_precision_profiling.py`
- **G3.** Rust/Candle port of one transformer-block forward pass, as a comprehension exercise for [[ignite-catalog]] — `parts/g_scaling_systems/g3_candle_transformer_port.py`
  - Python driver lives here; the Rust crate lives in rust/crates/ignite-port.

## H. Computer vision & OCR

*follows C; independent of D-G, so it can be taken straight after the ViT rung*

**Lab:** [open-mmlab/mmocr — detection and recognition reference implementations](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmocr)

Folder: `parts/h_computer_vision/`

- **H1.** Object detection from scratch — IoU, non-max suppression and mAP implemented by hand — `parts/h_computer_vision/h1_detection_from_scratch.py`
  - a single-stage detector on a small dataset; the metrics matter more than the backbone
- **H2.** Semantic segmentation with a U-Net — skip connections, Dice vs cross-entropy loss — `parts/h_computer_vision/h2_unet_segmentation.py`
- **H3.** Text recognition with CRNN + CTC — synthetic text lines, greedy vs beam decoding, CER/WER — `parts/h_computer_vision/h3_crnn_ctc.py`
  - CTC's alignment-free loss is the point: no per-character boxes needed
- **H4.** Attention-decoder OCR against CTC on the same data, with a pretrained model as the baseline — `parts/h_computer_vision/h4_attention_ocr.py`
  - TrOCR or EasyOCR as the reference; the comparison is decoder design, not dataset
- **H5.** Two-stage document pipeline — detect text regions, then recognize, with end-to-end error attributed to each stage — `parts/h_computer_vision/h5_document_pipeline.py`
